questions.question: In digital IC design, what is the primary purpose of a 'clock gating cell'?
options: To reduce dynamic power consumption by disabling clocks to inactive circuit blocks.
To synchronize asynchronous input signals to a clock domain.
To generate multiple clock phases from a single input clock.
To ensure proper timing closure by buffering high-fanout clock nets.
To provide a global reset signal for all sequential elements.

questions.question: In a CPU's memory management unit (MMU), what is the primary role of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
options: To cache recently used virtual-to-physical address translations.
To buffer data being written to main memory.
To store frequently executed instructions for faster retrieval.
To translate instruction opcodes into micro-operations.
To manage cache coherency across multiple cores.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of a 'scan chain' in the context of Design for Testability (DFT) for digital integrated circuits?
options: It provides a serial path to access and control the state of all sequential elements (flip-flops) during test mode.
It is a high-speed interface for communicating with external diagnostic equipment.
It synthesizes complex combinational logic into simpler gates.
It distributes clock signals to all parts of the chip with minimal skew.
It acts as a redundant backup path for critical data signals to improve reliability.

questions.question: In advanced Static Timing Analysis (STA) for deep submicron technologies, what is the primary challenge addressed by applying 'On-Chip Variation (OCV)' or 'timing derates'?
options: Accounting for variations in transistor performance and interconnect delays due to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) fluctuations across the chip.
Reducing the number of clock domains to simplify synchronization issues.
Minimizing the power consumption of the clock distribution network.
Preventing the generation of spurious clock signals due to noise.
Ensuring that all logic gates operate at their maximum possible frequency.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes 'Non-Volatile Memory' (NVM) from 'Volatile Memory'?
options: Non-Volatile Memory retains its stored information even when power is removed.
Non-Volatile Memory is significantly faster than Volatile Memory for read operations.
Non-Volatile Memory is typically used as the CPU's primary cache.
Non-Volatile Memory requires constant electrical refreshing to maintain data.
Non-Volatile Memory has a much smaller storage capacity compared to Volatile Memory.
